newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada updates financial instruments legislation.
newsitem.headline: Canada updates financial instruments legislation.

text.p: Canada moved to modernize its archaic financial instruments laws with the introduction of legislation on Thursday that establishes rights based on computerized rather than paper-based transactions.

The legislation creates two new classes of financial securities -- a depository bill and depository note -- allowing clearing houses or depositories to transfer these instruments from seller to buyer by recording entries on their books.
Under the current Bills of Exchange Act, clearing houses and depositories must be in physical possession of a negotiable instrument to record any transactions.
"The new way of proceeding will be better suited to the modern marketplace for these instruments," said Doug Peters on behalf of Canada's Minister of Finance Paul Martin.
The proposed legislation will also change certain aspects of the law to make it compatible with laws governing investment securities, said the Department of Finance.
